mainTopic: The duty to protest wrongdoing, the ת׳ marks in יחזקאל, the end of זכות אבות, and רב אמי's rule that death and suffering come from sin
overview: This עמוד is about responsibility for wrongdoing and about Divine justice. The גמרא first explains that the זקנים are judged because they did not protest against the sins of the שרים. A story follows: שמואל ignores a crying woman, and he explains that the main duty belongs to מר עוקבא, the אב בית דין from בית דוד. רבי זירא then tells רבי סימון to rebuke the ריש גלותא's household even if they will not listen. The proof is the story in יחזקאל of the ת׳ marks. The צדיקים were first protected, but מדת הדין argued that they could have protested and did not, so punishment began with them. The גמרא explains the bronze altar, the six destroying angels, and five meanings of the letter תיו. It then brings four opinions on when זכות אבות ended. Finally, רב אמי teaches that there is no death without sin and no suffering without sin, with a פסוק for each half. The גמרא will test this rule on the next עמוד.

steps.title: What did the Elders do wrong?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the זקנים are judged together with the princes, when it seems only the princes sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What sin did the Elders commit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is reading a פסוק (from earlier) in which God comes to judge both the elders and the princes. It asks: the princes sinned, but what did the elders do?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to punish the זקנים, the Sages, together with the שרים. But the Sages did not commit the sins themselves. So why should they be judged? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Elders, meaning the Sages of the generation

phrases.english: The Elders, what did they sin?
phrases.notes: This refers to the פסוק ה׳ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יָבוֹא עִם זִקְנֵי עַמּוֹ וְשָׂרָיו (ישעיהו 3:14), which was discussed on the previous עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the Isaiah פסוק from the earlier part of the sugya.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would the זקנים be judged if only the שרים actually sinned?

steps.title: The Elders are judged for not protesting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the פסוק: the Elders are judged because they did not protest against the princes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: God judges the Elders because they did not protest against the princes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading the פסוק differently. The Elders are judged because of their silence, not because they did the sins themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reading 'with the Elders' as if both groups committed the same sin, we read 'concerning the Elders'. Their sin was failing to protest (מחאה). This teaches that people with influence are responsible when they stay quiet in the face of wrongdoing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (read it this way instead)

steps.whatToRemember: A person who could protest a sin and stays silent is held responsible for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main idea that ties the whole passage together: leaders and Sages are responsible for wrongs they could have stopped.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Concerning the Elders, that they did not protest against the princes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The זקנים are punished for failing to protest against the שרים.

steps.title: שמואל ignores a crying woman
steps.stepSummary: A story: a woman cries out to שמואל about an injustice, and he pays no attention to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה was sitting before שמואל. A certain woman came and cried out before him, and he paid no attention to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that sets up the next move. רב יהודה sees his teacher שמואל ignore a woman crying for help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story fits the theme of leaders who fail to act. It is a setup: we expect someone to object to שמואל's behavior, and that is exactly what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting before him (as a student)

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda was sitting before Shmuel.
A certain woman came
crying out before him,
and he was not paying attention to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that illustrates the theme of leaders' responsibility.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: שמואל did not respond to a woman's cry.

steps.title: רב יהודה challenges שמואל with a verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks שמואל how he can ignore the poor, quoting a פסוק that says whoever does so will not be answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the master hold of the פסוק, 'Whoever closes his ear to the cry of the poor, he too will call out and not be answered'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה challenges his teacher. He quotes a פסוק from משלי that warns against ignoring the cry of the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that someone who ignores the poor will be ignored by Heaven when he himself cries out. שמואל's behavior seems to go directly against this. So רב יהודה asks how his teacher could act this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the master hold of this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לֵיהּ מָר:
phrases.english: He said to him: Does the master not hold:
"Whoever closes his ear to the cry of the poor,
phrases.notes: Proverbs 21:13

phrases.english: he too will call out and not be answered"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to שמואל's behavior in the story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק warns that whoever ignores the poor will be ignored by Heaven, so a judge should not ignore her.

steps.title: שמואל explains that מר עוקבא is responsible
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the main responsibility belongs to מר עוקבא, the אב בית דין, who will be punished more severely.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Sharp one! Your head (me, your teacher) will be punished in cold water, but the head of your head will be punished in hot water. מר עוקבא sits here as head of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defends himself. He says the main duty to handle this case belongs to מר עוקבא, who is the head of the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not deny that he has some responsibility; he admits he will be punished in 'cold water', a lighter punishment. But the person with real authority, מר עוקבא, carries the heavier 'hot water' punishment. Responsibility grows with the amount of power a person has.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharp one (a nickname for רב יהודה, literally 'big-toothed')
Your head (your superior, meaning your teacher)
Cold water / hot water (lighter and heavier punishment)

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying he is free of blame. He says his punishment is lighter ('cold'), while the person with more power gets the harsher one ('hot').

phrases.english: He said to him: Sharp one,
your head (superior) is in cold water,
the head of your head is in hot water.

phrases.aramaic: הָא יָתֵיב מָר עוּקְבָא אַב בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: Behold, Mar Ukva sits as head of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the main responsibility to the person with greater authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל, as the judge present, carries the full blame for ignoring the woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: מר עוקבא, the אב בית דין, carries the main responsibility, and שמואל only a lighter share.

steps.title: Verse showing the House of David must judge justly
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ירמיהו tells בית דוד to judge and save the robbed, which shows that this duty rests on the ריש גלותא's family, including מר עוקבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'House of David, so says ה׳: Judge justly in the morning, and save the robbed from the hand of the oppressor, lest My fury go out like fire and burn with no one to put it out, because of the evil of their deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for why מר עוקבא's family is responsible. The פסוק speaks directly to בית דוד, and the ריש גלותא's family descends from דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק orders the House of David to judge quickly and to rescue those who are robbed. It warns of a fierce punishment if they do not. This supports שמואל's claim that the 'hot water' punishment falls on מר עוקבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The House of David (the royal line; the ריש גלותא descends from it)

phrases.english: As it is written: "House of David, so says the Lord:
phrases.notes: Jeremiah 21:12

phrases.english: Execute judgment in the morning,
and save the robbed from the hand of the oppressor,
lest My fury go out like fire,
and burn with none to put it out,
because of the evil of their deeds, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for שמואל's answer.
steps.raayaObject: The House of the ריש גלותא, including מר עוקבא, holds the main duty to rescue the oppressed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Jeremiah 21:12, addressed to בית דוד, and the ריש גלותא descends from דוד.

steps.title: רבי זירא urges רבי סימון to rebuke the ריש גלותא's household
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רבי סימון to rebuke the members of the ריש גלותא's household.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי סימון: Let the master rebuke those of the house of the ריש גלותא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another story about rebuke. This is a setup: רבי זירא makes a request, and the next steps show the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי סימון had influence with the ריש גלותא's household, so רבי זירא felt he had a duty to correct them. This connects to the idea from step 2 that people with influence must protest wrongdoing.

keyTerms.meaning: Exilarch, the leader of the Jews in Babylonia

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי סִימוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Simon:
Let the master rebuke
those of the house of the Exilarch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי סִימוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story on the duty of rebuke.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone with influence should rebuke the ריש גלותא's household.

steps.title: Rabbi Simon objects that they will not listen
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימון answers that the household will not accept rebuke from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They will not accept it from me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי סימון pushes back. He argues that rebuking them is pointless because they will not listen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumes the purpose of rebuke is to change behavior, so if it will not work, there is no need to give it. The next step rejects this assumption.

phrases.english: He said to him: They will not accept it from me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבי זירא's instruction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's instruction to rebuke the household.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rebuke that will certainly be rejected seems useless, so there should be no obligation to give it.

steps.title: Rebuke them even if they will not accept
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא insists that רבי סימון must rebuke them even if they will not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even though they will not accept, let the master rebuke them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא rejects the objection. He says that the duty to rebuke remains even when it will not be accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obligation to protest does not depend on success. Like the זקנים in step 2, someone who stays silent shares the blame, even if speaking up would not have changed anything. The גמרא will next bring a source for this idea.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי זירא, the duty of תוכחה applies even when the listener will probably reject it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises the key question of whether one must rebuke when it will not help. Steps 10–16 prove רבי זירא's view through the story of the תיו marks.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Even though they will not accept,
let the master rebuke them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי סימון's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption that the duty depends on success
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If rebuke will not be accepted, one need not give it.
steps.terutzMaskana: One must rebuke even when it will not be accepted.

steps.title: The one good decree that was taken back
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא never reversed a good decree into a bad one, except in the case of the mark in יחזקאל chapter 9.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אחא ברבי חנינא said: Never did a good decree come out of the mouth of הקדוש ברוך הוא and then get reversed for bad, except in this case. As the פסוק says: 'And ה׳ said to him: Go through the city, through ירושלים, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry over all the disgusting things done there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching to support רבי זירא's point that you must rebuke even when it may not help. This line opens the story that will prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דאמר' ('as he said') tells us this teaching is brought as backing for what came before. רבי אחא says this is the only case where a good decree was reversed. The rest of the story will show that the reason was a failure to rebuke.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall mark a ת׳ (a sign)
Those who sigh and cry out in pain

phrases.english: As Rabbi Aha son of Rabbi Hanina said:
phrases.notes: 'As he said' means this teaching backs up רבי זירא's statement.

phrases.english: Never did a good decree go out
from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He
and He then reversed it for bad
except for this matter,
as it is written: "And the Lord said to him:
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 9:4

phrases.english: Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem,
and put a mark (tav) on the foreheads of the men
who sigh and who cry out

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת הַנַּעֲשׂוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: over all the abominations that are done in its midst, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי זירא's insistence in Step 9 that one must rebuke even when it will not be accepted.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's ruling that one must rebuke even if the rebuke will not be accepted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא's teaching about the mark in יחזקאל 9:4

steps.title: Ink for the righteous, blood for the wicked
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells גבריאל to mark the צדיקים with an ink ת׳ for protection and the רשעים with a blood ת׳ so they will be punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to גבריאל: Go and write a ת׳ of ink on the foreheads of the צדיקים, so the angels of destruction cannot harm them. And write a ת׳ of blood on the foreheads of the רשעים, so the angels of destruction can harm them.
steps.whatsHappening: The story explains the פסוק. This is the original good decree: the צדיקים get a protective mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two marks are given. The ink mark protects and the blood mark allows punishment. The 'good decree' that will later be reversed is the protection of the צדיקים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְגַבְרִיאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Gabriel:

phrases.aramaic: לֵךְ וּרְשׁוֹם עַל מִצְחָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים
phrases.english: Go and write on the foreheads of the righteous
a tav of ink,
so that the angels of destruction will not have power over them.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל מִצְחָם שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים תָּיו שֶׁל דָּם
phrases.english: And on the foreheads of the wicked, a tav of blood,
so that the angels of destruction will have power over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְגַבְרִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in Step 10 and describes the original good decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צדיקים were originally marked for protection and the רשעים were marked for punishment.

steps.title: Justice asks what separates the two groups
steps.stepSummary: מדת הדין asks הקדוש ברוך הוא why these people are treated differently from those.
steps.simpleTranslation: מדת הדין said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world! What makes these different from those?
steps.whatsHappening: מדת הדין asks what the difference between the two groups is. This sets up the argument that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface this is a simple question. It opens the door for מדת הדין to argue that the צדיקים share some of the blame.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה מִדַּת הַדִּין לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The attribute of justice said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe!
How are these different from those?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the two different marks given in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the difference between the two groups that justifies different treatment?

steps.title: One group is fully righteous, the other fully wicked
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers that one group is made up of צדיקים גמורים and the other of רשעים גמורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: These are completely righteous, and those are completely wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers the question: the difference is simply their behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the צדיקים did nothing wrong themselves. This sets up מדת הדין's next point, which is that sins of omission also count.

phrases.english: He said to her: These are completely righteous,
and those are completely wicked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is that one group is fully righteous and the other is fully wicked.

steps.title: They could have protested and did not
steps.stepSummary: מדת הדין objects that the צדיקים had the ability to protest against the רשעים and failed to do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said before Him: Master of the world! It was in their power to protest, and they did not protest!
steps.whatsHappening: מדת הדין challenges the claim that the צדיקים are blameless. They stayed silent when they could have spoken up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being personally righteous is not enough. If you are able to protest wrongdoing and do not, you carry responsibility. This is the core idea behind רבי זירא's instruction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the responsibility of מחאה (protesting wrongdoing). It explains why רבי סימון cannot stay quiet.

phrases.english: She said before Him: Master of the Universe!
It was in their power to protest,
and they did not protest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 13 that the צדיקים are fully righteous.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the צדיקים are blameless
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Failing to protest when one is able to is itself a fault, so the צדיקים are not fully innocent.

steps.title: Their protest would not have worked anyway
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers that He knows the רשעים would not have accepted the protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: It is revealed and known before Me that if they had protested, the רשעים would not have accepted it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא defends the צדיקים: their protest would have been useless, so their silence did not change anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense is that the duty to protest applies only when it can help. This is the same argument רבי סימון made in Step 8: 'they will not accept it from me.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is revealed and known before Me

phrases.english: He said to her: It is revealed and known before Me
that if they had protested against them,
they would not have accepted it from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes blame by showing the protest would have been useless
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The צדיקים are guilty for not protesting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their silence did not matter because the רשעים would not have listened.

steps.title: You knew it would fail, but did they?
steps.stepSummary: מדת הדין argues back: even if הקדוש ברוך הוא knew the protest would fail, the צדיקים did not know that.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said before Him: Master of the world! If it is revealed before You, is it revealed to them?
steps.whatsHappening: מדת הדין knocks down the defense. Only ה׳ knew the protest would fail, and the צדיקים had no such knowledge, so they should have tried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot excuse himself from rebuking just because it might not work, since he cannot know the outcome for sure. This answers רבי סימון's excuse from Step 8 and proves רבי זירא's ruling in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is revealed before You

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think מדת הדין is saying the protest would have worked. She accepts that it would have failed. Her point is that the צדיקים could not have known that, so they were still obligated to try.
steps.whatToRemember: One must rebuke wrongdoing even when it seems useless, because a human cannot be certain it will fail. This is why רבי סימון must rebuke the ריש גלותא's household.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the classic source that the uncertainty of results does not cancel the obligation of תוכחה.

phrases.english: She said before Him: Master of the Universe!
phrases.notes: The text is corrected from masculine 'אמר' to feminine 'אמרה', since the speaker is מדת הדין.

phrases.english: If it is revealed before You,
is it revealed to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם לְפָנֶיךָ גָּלוּי לָהֶם מִי גָּלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense of Step 15 and thereby supports רבי זירא's ruling against רבי סימון's excuse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The excuse that the protest would not have been accepted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The צדיקים could not know their protest would fail, so they were obligated to try.

steps.title: The verse shows the punishment began with the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings verses from יחזקאל that show the destroyers were told to begin at 'My Sanctuary', with the elders before the House.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what the verse means: 'Old man, young man, maiden, little children and women, slay utterly; but do not come near anyone who has the mark on him; and begin from My Sanctuary.' And it is also written: 'And they began with the elderly men who were before the House.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows from a פסוק that מדת הדין's argument was accepted. The punishment really did start with the leaders standing at the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 ended with מדת הדין saying the צדיקים should have protested anyway. These verses show the result: the destroyers began 'from My Sanctuary', with the elders before the House. The next step explains that these elders are the צדיקים themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written. It ties a story to a פסוק
A mark or sign, here the letter תיו

phrases.english: And that is what is written:
"Old man, young man, and maiden,
little children and women, slay utterly;

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כׇּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו הַתָּו
phrases.english: but upon any man who has the mark on him
do not come near;
and begin from My Sanctuary."
And it is written: "And they began with the elderly men
who were before the House."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל ט:ו

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows from a פסוק that מדת הדין's final argument won
steps.raayaObject: That the צדיקים who failed to protest were punished first

steps.title: Read 'My sanctified ones' instead of 'My Sanctuary'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reads the word מקדשי as מקודשי, meaning the people who kept the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: Do not read 'My Sanctuary' (מקדשי). Read instead 'My sanctified ones' (מקודשי). These are people who kept the entire תורה, from א to ת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains who the 'Sanctuary' in the פסוק really refers to. It means the holy people, the צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using an אל תקרי reading, the place becomes people. So 'begin from My Sanctuary' means 'begin from My most righteous ones'. This makes the פסוק fit the story exactly: the complete צדיקים were punished first for not protesting.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as X, rather read it as Y. A דרשה on the vowels of a word
From א to ת, meaning completely

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not change the written text of the פסוק. It adds a second layer of meaning on top of the simple reading.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
Do not read "My Sanctuary"
rather "My sanctified ones"
these are people who fulfilled
the entire Torah
from alef to tav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the key word of the פסוק just quoted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'My Sanctuary' refers to the complete צדיקים who kept the entire תורה

steps.title: Immediately the six destroyers arrive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing six men with weapons and one man in linen coming to stand by the bronze altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: And immediately: 'And behold, six men came from the upper gate, which faces north. Each man had his weapon of destruction in his hand. One man among them was dressed in linen, with a scribe's inkwell at his waist. They came and stood beside the bronze altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that once the decision was made, punishment came right away. This פסוק also sets up the next questions about the 'bronze altar' and the 'six men'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ומיד stresses how fast the judgment was carried out. This step is mainly a setup: it introduces the details that the גמרא will now ask about.

phrases.english: And immediately:
"And behold, six men were coming
from the way of the upper gate
which faces north,
each man with his weapon of destruction in his hand,
and one man among them dressed in linen,
with a scribe's inkwell at his waist;
and they came and stood
beside the bronze altar."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל ט:ב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and sets up the next questions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The punishment came immediately through six destroyers

steps.title: Was there really a bronze altar then?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the פסוק: there was no bronze altar in the time of יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there a bronze altar back then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a difficulty in the פסוק. Since שלמה's time the altar was made of stone, so what 'bronze altar' could this be?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge to the simple reading. It forces a non-literal explanation, which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Was there a bronze altar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a detail of the פסוק just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'bronze altar' in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No bronze altar was in use in the בית המקדש in יחזקאל's time, so a literal reading does not work

steps.title: Begin where they sing before Me
steps.stepSummary: The 'bronze altar' hints to the place of the לויים' song, so the punishment begins there.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to them: Begin from the place where they say song before Me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'bronze altar' is a hint, not a literal object. It points to the place where the לויים sang, whose instruments were made of bronze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the פסוק is really telling the destroyers where to start. They start with the holiest people, the ones who sing before ה׳. This matches רב יוסף's point that punishment began with the 'sanctified ones'.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
Begin from the place
where they say song before Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: הַתְחִילוּ מִמְּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the bronze-altar difficulty
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: a figure of speech, not a literal altar
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק refers to an actual bronze altar, which did not exist
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a hint to begin from the place of the לויים' song

steps.title: Who are the six men?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the six men in the vision are.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who are the six men?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question about another detail in the פסוק. This sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no difficulty here, only a request for identification. The answer will show that they are not ordinary people.

phrases.english: And who are the six men?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another detail of the same פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the six men

steps.title: Six angels of destruction
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא names the six men as six destroying forces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Fury, Anger, Rage, Destroyer, Breaker, and Annihilator.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the six 'men' are six angels of punishment. Each one is named for a kind of destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'men' are really מלאכי חבלה, agents of Divine anger. This shows how severe the judgment was.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Fury, Anger, and Rage,
and Destroyer, and Breaker, and Annihilator.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the six men
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are six angels of destruction

steps.title: Why specifically the letter תיו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the mark on people's foreheads was the letter תיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about the letter תיו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the 'mark' in the פסוק and asks why it was a תיו. This sets up a series of answers from different אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several Sages will answer, each with his own idea. Most of them treat the תיו as the first letter of a meaningful word.

phrases.english: And what is different about "tav"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the 'mark' mentioned in the earlier פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind choosing the letter תיו

steps.title: רב: תיו for live and תיו for die
steps.stepSummary: רב says the תיו stands for תחיה (you will live) for the צדיקים and תמות (you will die) for the רשעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: תיו stands for תחיה, 'you shall live'. And תיו stands for תמות, 'you shall die'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that the same letter carried two opposite messages. One group would live and the other would die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the earlier story, the צדיקים got a תיו of ink for life and the רשעים a תיו of blood for death. One letter can open both words, so it fits both groups.

phrases.english: Rav said:
"Tav": you shall live;
"Tav": you shall die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to why a תיו
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תיו is the first letter of both תחיה and תמות

steps.title: שמואל: the merit of the fathers has ended
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the תיו stands for תמה, meaning זכות אבות has run out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The merit of the fathers has ended.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second reason for the תיו. It signals that the merit of the אבות can no longer protect them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the letter does not split into life and death. It sends one message: זכות אבות will not save them now.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The merit of the fathers has ended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer from רב's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תיו stands for תמה: זכות אבות has ended

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the merit of the fathers will bring mercy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the תיו stands for תחון, meaning ה׳ will show mercy because of זכות אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The merit of the fathers will bring mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third reason, which is almost the opposite of שמואל's. The תיו says זכות אבות will still bring mercy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the merit has run out. For רבי יוחנן, it still works, and ה׳ will have mercy on the צדיקים because of it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The merit of the fathers will bring mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with שמואל's view
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תיו stands for תחון: זכות אבות will bring mercy

steps.title: ריש לקיש: תיו ends ה׳'s seal of truth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says תיו is the last letter of ה׳'s seal, אמת, as רבי חנינא taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: תיו is the end of the seal of הקדוש ברוך הוא. As רבי חנינא said: The seal of הקדוש ברוך הוא is 'אמת', truth.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a fourth reason. He supports it with רבי חנינא's teaching that ה׳'s seal is the word אמת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the others, ריש לקיש looks at the last letter of a word, not the first. The ת closes the word אמת, so the mark shows that this judgment is sealed with ה׳'s truth.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
"Tav" is the end of the seal
of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as Rabbi Chanina said:
The seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is "truth".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer, based on the last letter of a word
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תיו is the last letter of אמת‎, ה׳'s seal

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: they kept the תורה from א to ת
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says the תיו marks people who kept the entire תורה from א to ת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: These are people who kept the entire תורה, from א to ת.
steps.whatsHappening: The last answer says the תיו marks complete צדיקים. They kept the whole תורה, from its first letter to its last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the wording used earlier by רב יוסף, but here it explains the תיו itself. The letter that ends the alphabet stands for complete תורה observance.
steps.whatToRemember: There are five readings of the תיו. רב: life or death. שמואל: זכות אבות has ended. רבי יוחנן: זכות אבות brings mercy. ריש לקיש: the end of ה׳'s seal, אמת. רבי שמואל בר נחמני: they kept the whole תורה from א to ת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
phrases.notes: Text variant: the word אמר appears in parentheses before the name and in brackets after it

phrases.english: These are people who fulfilled
the entire Torah
from alef to tav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final answer in the list of explanations for the תיו
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תיו marks people who kept the entire תורה from א to ת

steps.title: From when did the merit of the Forefathers end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא follows up on שמואל's idea that זכות אבות has ended and asks when that happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when did the merit of the Forefathers come to an end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that sets up the next four steps. If זכות אבות ran out, at what point in history did that happen?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the תיו means 'תמה', that זכות אבות is finished. That raises a natural follow-up: when did it finish? The answers come in the next steps, each from a different אמורא.

keyTerms.meaning: The merit of the Forefathers (אברהם, יצחק, יעקב) that protects their descendants

phrases.english: From when did the merit of the Forefathers end?
phrases.notes: Builds on שמואל's explanation of the תיו as 'תמה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side discussion based on שמואל's interpretation of the תיו in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The point in history when זכות אבות stopped protecting Israel.

steps.title: רב: From the days of הושע בן בארי
steps.stepSummary: רב says זכות אבות ended in the time of the נביא הושע, based on the פסוק 'no man will save her from My hand'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: from the days of הושע בן בארי, as it says: 'I will uncover her shame before her lovers, and no man will save her from My hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. זכות אבות ended in the days of the נביא הושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In הושע's prophecy, ה׳ says that 'no man' will rescue Israel from His punishment. רב reads this as saying that the merit of the אבות will no longer save Israel, because that merit has been used up.

keyTerms.meaning: The נביא הושע, son of בארי
And no man will save her

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: מִימוֹת הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן בְּאֵרִי,
phrases.english: Rav said: from the days of Hoshea son of Be'eri,
as it is said: 'I will uncover her shame'
phrases.notes: הושע 2:12

phrases.english: before the eyes of her lovers
and no man will save her from My hand.'
phrases.notes: No one, not even the merit of the אבות, will save her anymore.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מִימוֹת הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן בְּאֵרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זכות אבות ended in the days of הושע בן בארי.

steps.title: שמואל: From the days of חזאל
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says זכות אבות ended in the days of חזאל, king of ארם, since the פסוק says ה׳ protected Israel because of the אבות 'until now'.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: from the days of חזאל, as it says: 'חזאל king of ארם oppressed Israel all the days of יהואחז.' And it is written: 'ה׳ was gracious to them and had mercy on them, and turned to them because of His covenant with אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב. He did not want to destroy them, and He did not cast them away from before Him until now.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second answer. זכות אבות ended in the time of חזאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ saved Israel from חזאל because of the אבות 'עד עתה', 'until now'. שמואל reads 'until now' as a time limit: up to this point the אבות protected them, but not after. This is also the last time the פסוקים mention ה׳ saving Israel because of the אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: חזאל, king of ארם, who oppressed Israel
And it is written (introduces a second פסוק)
For the sake of His covenant
Until now. Read as a time limit.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: from the days of Chazael,
as it is said: 'And Chazael king of Aram'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 13:22

phrases.aramaic: לָחַץ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כֹּל יְמֵי יְהוֹאָחָז״.
phrases.english: oppressed Israel all the days of Yehoachaz.'
And it is written: 'And ה׳ was gracious to them and had mercy on them,'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 13:23

phrases.english: and turned to them for the sake of His covenant
with Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov,
and He did not want to destroy them,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִשְׁלִיכָם מֵעַל פָּנָיו עַד עָתָּה״.
phrases.english: and He did not cast them away from before Him until now.'
phrases.notes: 'Until now' means up to this point, and not afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the question in Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זכות אבות ended in the days of חזאל, as shown by 'עד עתה'.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: From the days of אליהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says זכות אבות ended in the days of אליהו, at the showdown on הר הכרמל, based on the word 'today'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: from the days of אליהו, as it says: 'When it was time for the afternoon offering, אליהו the נביא came close and said: ה׳, God of אברהם, יצחק, and ישראל, today let it be known that You are God in Israel, and I am Your servant, and by Your word I have done all these things.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a third answer. זכות אבות ended in the time of אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו calls on the God of the אבות and asks that it be known 'today'. רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'הַיּוֹם' as saying: today the merit of the אבות still works, but after today it will not. So אליהו used up the last of it at הר הכרמל.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of the afternoon offering
Today let it be known. 'Today' hints: only today, not afterward.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: מִימֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: from the days of Eliyahu,
as it is said: 'And it was at the time of the afternoon offering,'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:36

phrases.english: Eliyahu the prophet came close and said:
ה׳, God of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yisrael,

phrases.aramaic: הַיּוֹם יִוָּדַע כִּי אַתָּה אֱלֹהִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: today let it be known that You are God in Israel,
phrases.notes: 'Today', but not afterward.

phrases.english: and I am Your servant,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִדְבָרְךָ עָשִׂיתִי [אֵת] כׇּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and by Your word I have done all these things, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: מִימֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, competing answer to the question in Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זכות אבות ended in the days of אליהו, as shown by 'today'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: From the days of חזקיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says זכות אבות ended in the days of חזקיהו. From then on, only ה׳'s own 'zeal' would act for Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: from the days of חזקיהו, as it says: 'For the growth of the kingdom and for peace without end, on the throne of דוד and on his kingdom, to set it up and support it with justice and righteousness, from now and forever, the zeal of ה׳ of Hosts will do this.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the fourth and last answer. זכות אבות ended in the time of חזקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק, said about חזקיהו's time, says that 'from now on' what protects the kingdom is 'the zeal of ה׳'. The אבות are not mentioned. רבי יוחנן reads this to mean that from then on Israel is saved only by ה׳'s own zeal, not by the merit of the אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: חזקיהו, the righteous king of יהודה
The zeal of ה׳ of Hosts. ה׳ acts on His own, not because of the אבות.

steps.whatToRemember: There are four opinions on when זכות אבות ended: רב says הושע, שמואל says חזאל, רבי יהושע בן לוי says אליהו, and רבי יוחנן says חזקיהו. Each one reads a פסוק as marking a cutoff point ('no man will save', 'until now', 'today', 'from now on').
steps.confusionAlert: Earlier (Step 27), רבי יוחנן said זכות אבות still exists ('תחון'). Yet here he gives a date for when it ended. Don't think he is simply contradicting himself. The מפרשים (e.g., תוספות) explain that the merit of the אבות ended, but the covenant (ברית) with the אבות never ends.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: from the days of Chizkiyahu,
as it is said: 'For the growth of the kingdom'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 9:6

phrases.english: and for peace without end,
on the throne of David and on his kingdom,
to set it up and to support it
with justice and with righteousness;
from now and forever,
phrases.notes: 'From now on', a new period begins.

phrases.aramaic: קִנְאַת ה׳ צְבָאוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה זֹּאת וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: the zeal of ה׳ of Hosts will do this, etc.'
phrases.notes: Only ה׳'s zeal, not the merit of the אבות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth, competing answer to the question in Step 30. It ends the list of opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זכות אבות ended in the days of חזקיהו. From then on, only 'קנאת ה׳' acts for Israel.

steps.title: No death without sin and no suffering without sin
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי teaches two rules: a person does not die unless he sinned, and a person does not suffer unless he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי said: There is no death without sin, and there is no suffering without sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב אמי about why people die and why people suffer. It does not yet give any proof; the proofs come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אמי makes two separate claims. Death is always caused by a person's own sin, and suffering is always caused by a person's own sin. This continues the theme of reward, punishment and merit from the previous steps about זכות אבות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a strong and sweeping claim. Steps 36 and 37 bring a פסוק for each half. On the next עמוד the גמרא tests it against other sources to see whether it can really stand. Remember both halves clearly, because each half gets its own proof and its own discussion.

phrases.english: Rav Ami said:
There is no death without sin,
phrases.notes: Rule #1: a person dies only because he sinned.

phrases.english: and there is no suffering without iniquity.
phrases.notes: Rule #2: a person suffers only because he sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי: אֵין מִיתָה בְּלֹא חֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of when זכות אבות ended to a new, related principle about divine justice: death and suffering come from sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Death comes only because of sin, and suffering comes only because of sin.

steps.title: A verse showing that death comes from sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the first rule, that there is no death without sin, from the פסוק in יחזקאל: 'the soul that sins, it shall die'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is no death without sin' is learned from the פסוק: 'The soul that sins, it shall die. A son will not carry the sin of the father, and a father will not carry the sin of the son. The righteousness of the righteous will be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked will be upon him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the first half of רב אמי's statement and brings a פסוק to back it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links dying directly to sinning: 'the soul that sins, it shall die.' It also says each person is judged for his own actions, not his father's or son's. So when a person dies, it is because of his own sin.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written; introduces a פסוק as a source
The righteousness of the righteous person
'And so on', meaning the פסוק continues (abbreviated וְגוֹ׳)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא repeats the words 'אין מיתה בלא חטא' here. This is not a new statement. It is a label telling you which half of רב אמי's rule is about to be proven.

phrases.english: There is no death without sin — as it is written:
phrases.notes: Quotes rule #1 again in order to prove it.

phrases.english: "The soul that sins, it shall die;
phrases.notes: The key words: sinning leads to death (יחזקאל יח:כ).

phrases.english: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father,
neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son;
phrases.notes: Each person is judged for his own sins.

phrases.english: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him,
and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for the first half of רב אמי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רב אמי's rule that there is no death without sin

steps.title: A verse showing that suffering comes from sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the second rule, that there is no suffering without sin, from the פסוק in תהלים: 'I will punish their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with strokes'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is no suffering without sin' is learned from the פסוק: 'And I will punish their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with plagues.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the second half of רב אמי's statement and brings a פסוק to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes ה׳ bringing pain, the 'rod' and the 'plagues', as a response to 'their transgression' and 'their iniquity'. This shows that suffering comes because of sin. Together with the previous step, both halves of רב אמי's statement now have a source.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will punish (literally, 'I will visit upon')
A rod or stick used to strike

steps.whatToRemember: רב אמי holds that death and suffering are both caused by sin. Death is proven from 'הנפש החוטאת היא תמות', and suffering is proven from 'ופקדתי בשבט פשעם ובנגעים עונם'.

phrases.english: There is no suffering without iniquity — as it is written:
phrases.notes: Quotes rule #2 again in order to prove it.

phrases.english: "Then I will punish their transgression with the rod,
phrases.notes: תהלים פט:לג

phrases.english: and their iniquity with strokes."
phrases.notes: Suffering (strokes) comes as a result of sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to the previous step: supplies the scriptural source for the second half of רב אמי's statement.
